read: full: all 17 pages (abstract, sections 1-7, references, appendices A-E on prompt, step weights, extraction pipeline and significance tests).
venue_now: arXiv preprint 2604.19758v1 [cs.AI], dated 25 March 2026 (p.1 margin stamp; the title page says 'March 2026'); single author (Olivenet, Kyrenia, Cyprus); no venue shown.
what_it_is: ThermoQA is an engineering-thermodynamics benchmark of 293 open-ended numerical problems in three tiers: property lookups (110), component analysis across seven device types (101) and full cycle analysis across ten cycle types (82), with water, R-134a and variable-cp air (p.1, p.3-4). Question parameters are sampled programmatically from realistic ranges, and every answer, including each intermediate state value, is computed with CoolProp 7.2.0 and NASA polynomials; there are no hand-authored solutions (p.2, p.4). Tiers 2 and 3 are scored step by step: each of 5-12 (Tier 2) or 15-60 (Tier 3) intermediate and final quantities is extracted from the free-text response and counted correct within +/-2% or +/-0.5, weighted by engineering importance (p.3-4). Six frontier models are run three times each, and run-to-run standard deviations are reported (p.5-6, p.10).
domain: engineering: thermodynamics (mechanical and chemical engineering), with water, R-134a and air
size: 293 questions (Tier 1 110, Tier 2 101, Tier 3 82); 6 models x 3 runs x 3 tiers = 54 evaluation runs, about 5,300 API calls (p.1, p.5).
source_of_items: generated from templates: parameters (pressures, temperatures, efficiencies, flow rates) sampled from physically realistic ranges and checked for feasibility, with outlet states derived by conservation equations (an 'anchor-derive pattern'); ground truth computed with CoolProp and NASA 7-coefficient polynomials (p.4).
instances: generated, then released as one fixed public set of 293 questions (p.1-2, p.4). The paper says the pipeline 'can produce new question instances indefinitely' (p.3, p.14), but the evaluation uses only the released set.
has_gold_traces: partial: a code-computed reference value for every scored intermediate and final quantity, with weights (Tier 2 5-12 steps, Tier 3 15-60 steps; Appendix C lists them) (p.3-4, p.15-16). There is no written worked solution.
evaluation: step-level or process, deterministic: Tier 1 per-property tolerance; Tiers 2-3 score the weighted fraction of intermediate and final quantities within +/-2% relative or +/-0.5 absolute, with +/-0.02 for efficiencies and COP (p.4). Values are extracted from the free-text response, thinking tokens included, by regex and by gpt-4.1-mini, and a step counts as correct if either extraction is (take-max) (p.5, p.16-17). Each model is run three times, with Welch t-tests between models (p.5-6, p.17).
human_validation: None of items or evaluator. The ground truth is programmatic ('eliminating human annotation error', 'No hand-authored solutions', p.2), checked against NIST: '<0.01%' on p.2, and '<0.037% maximum deviation across 13 saturation points' for water on p.4. The extraction pipeline is not checked against humans; the paper reports only that LLM extraction raised aggregate scores by 1-3% over regex (p.17).
contamination_measures: generated instances: parameters are sampled programmatically ('reducing memorization risk'), but the problem structures follow textbook patterns and 'data contamination from training corpora cannot be fully excluded' (p.13). The 293-question set is public on Hugging Face (p.1-2). Regeneration is offered as future resilience (p.14).

engtrace_use.explanation: Candidate; the May paper does not cite it, and it does not cite EngTrace. It is the closest single-domain precedent for EngTrace's milestone check: intermediate values computed by code and checked deterministically against a tolerance in the model's free-text answer (p.4-5), with repeated runs (p.10). It also contradicts the May claim that engineering benchmarks 'remain limited to outcome matching'.

suggested_wording: ThermoQA (Duzkar, 2026) computes the answers to 293 engineering-thermodynamics problems, intermediate states included, with CoolProp and scores the weighted fraction of intermediate values within a 2% tolerance over three runs per model; it covers one domain, releases a single fixed question set, and neither its extraction nor its scoring is checked against human judgement.
facts_to_cite: 293 open-ended problems in three tiers: property lookups (110), component analysis (101), cycle analysis (82), with water, R-134a and variable-cp air (p.1, p.3-4)
Question parameters sampled programmatically; all answers, including intermediate states, computed with CoolProp 7.2.0 and NASA polynomials, with no hand-authored solutions (p.2, p.4)
Tiers 2-3 scored as a weighted fraction of 5-12 or 15-60 intermediate and final quantities within +/-2% or +/-0.5 of the computed values (p.3-4)
Values are extracted from free text by regex and an LLM (gpt-4.1-mini), taking whichever extraction is correct (p.5, p.17)
Six frontier models, three runs each; run-to-run standard deviations from 0.1 to 2.5 points (p.5, p.10)
Scores fall from Tier 1 to Tier 3 by 2.8 to 32.5 points across models (p.6-7)
The author notes contamination 'cannot be fully excluded' because problem structures follow textbook patterns (p.13)
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares: an engineering domain (thermodynamics, part of EngTrace's chemical and mechanical branches); parameters sampled programmatically with ground truth computed by code (p.4); deterministic tolerance checks of intermediate values read from the model's free text, the design of EngTrace's milestone check (p.4-5); three tiers (p.3-4); repeated runs with reported variance (p.10), like EngTrace's decoding repeats. Lacks: multi-branch scope (one domain); renewable or private instances (one public fixed set of 293, p.1-2); per-claim arithmetic consistency checks (self-inconsistency is noted only qualitatively, p.12); any expert validation of items, extraction or scoring; a judge or other way to credit a valid alternative path, since a step counts only if the reported value matches the reference. What EngTrace adds beyond it: five branches and 150 templates with a private-seed pool, per-claim recomputation of the arithmetic the trace displays, a residual judge for milestones the deterministic check misses, and validation of the whole evaluator against 15 experts' labels.
notes: (1) The web search note's 'The set is static' is half right: the questions are generated programmatically (p.4) but evaluated as one released fixed set; do not describe ThermoQA as hand-written or as dynamically regenerated. (2) The take-max extraction credits a step if either the regex or the LLM pass finds the correct value, and the LLM reads thinking tokens too (p.5, p.17); the scoring is therefore lenient by design. (3) Disclosure: the benchmark was built with Claude's help and Claude Opus 4.6 ranks first, which the author flags (p.13-14). (4) NIST agreement is stated as '<0.01%' (p.2) and as '<0.037% maximum deviation' (p.4). (5) The v1 date (25 March 2026) precedes its April identifier, as the web note says. (6) The 'Depth C' paradox (scores rise with added exergy steps) is attributed to the weighting (p.9, p.13), a caution for any weighted milestone score.
